subject: Food Science
title: The Green Revolution
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Green Revolution.

hook.text: Norman Borlaug's dwarf wheat varieties saved an estimated 1 billion people from starvation. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

buildup.text: In the 1960s, famine threatened India and Pakistan. Borlaug bred short, sturdy wheat plants that channeled energy into grain.

discovery.text: His wheat produced 3–4 times more grain per acre. India went from importing millions of tons to self-sufficiency in wheat by 1974.

twist.text: The Green Revolution required synthetic fertilizers and irrigation—creating dependence on fossil fuels and depleting aquifers.

climax.text: The Green Revolution matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Shorter plants, bigger harvests, a billion lives saved.

quiz.question: What made Borlaug's wheat varieties so productive?
options: Short, sturdy plants that channeled energy into grain instead of tall stalks—producing 3–4x more per acre
